newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end limit down, limits expanded.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end limit down, limits expanded.

text.p: November and January CME lumber futures remained locked down the $10.00 per tbf daily limit for the second consecutive trading day at the close, which set the stage for an expanded $15.00 daily limit on Tuesday.

November ended limit down at $351.00 per tbf and January limit down at $340.00. Other months finished $4.90 to $1.00 lower. There were 500 unfilled sell orders in November and the synthetic option was $10.00 lower at the close.
Heavy speculative and fund liquidation selling rolled over from Friday's limit decline with weak fundamental and technical factors prompting the recent break, traders said.

Cash market turned quiet and expectations are for cash lumber prices to start falling. November and the holiday period into January is usually a slow period for the lumber market as winter weather curbs construction projects in some parts of the United States, they said.
"By mid to late week you are going to see much lower lumber prices," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Technicals also pointed much lower after penetrating major chart support levels.
"They broke the 40-day moving average," a trader said.
